personality_one_liner: A high-performance, dark-mode command center focused on high-contrast operational clarity, speed, and precision for Base-6 (Seximal) computing and timekeeping.

spacing.rule: Use tight, operational spacing. Dividers and tonal separation over heavy shadows. Maintain comfortable hit areas (min 44pt) without wasting screen real estate.

do's: Use standard flat/tonal surfaces to maintain pure utility and high contrast
dont's: Do not use blur or glass on data/calculator screens; clarity and speed beat aesthetics here

screens.name: Calc
screens.purpose: A base-6 only calculator with keypad 0-5 and operators.
screens.layout: Top half displays current input (large Barlow Condensed) and calculation history (smaller, muted text above it). Bottom half is a rigid flex grid keypad. Numbers 0-5 and operators. Operators use brandSecondary tinted buttons or text. Use brandPrimary for the equals/evaluate button. Instant touch haptics on every key press.

screens.name: Convert

states.loading: Skeleton of the stacked conversion cards.

screens.layout: Two vertically stacked, distinct structural blocks ('From' at top, 'To' at bottom) separated by a subtle divider. No standard wheel pickers. Tap a block to slide open an inline/nested list to pick Category (Length/Time/Mass) -> Unit -> Prefix. The numerical output updates instantaneously in the bottom block. Use surfaceSecondary for the blocks and brandPrimary for the currently selected unit highlight.

screens.name: Time
screens.purpose: Seximal clock, timer, and stopwatch based on iOS Clock app.
screens.layout: Segmented control at the top to toggle (Clock / Timer / Stopwatch). Clock: Digital display using massive Barlow Condensed digits, showing Hours, New Minutes, New Seconds. Timer: Large circular progress ring in brandPrimary, counting down. A muted contextual 'Ends at X' label above the countdown. Stopwatch: Millisecond precision with drag-cancellable buttons. Split laps listed below in a scrolling list, emphasizing the fastest/slowest laps using success/error color tints on the text.

screens.name: Learn
screens.purpose: Educational reference for Seximal math and units.
screens.layout: Editorial-meets-utility. A top hero image (abstract math/geometry) with a gradient scrim. Followed by a scrolling feed of `surfaceSecondary` cards explaining base-6, base conversions, and the custom unit list (instants, bocks, nifa-, kila-). Use tables or strictly aligned flex rows for the unit references so it's easy to scan.

learn_hero.alt: Dark abstract math geometry with warm amber glowing curves

timer_accent.alt: Abstract long-exposure light painting spiral in amber/orange

instructions_to_main_agent: Design constraint: Implement Tab Navigation with exactly 4 tabs (Calc, Convert, Time, Learn). Use Phosphor icons.

Style constraint: Strictly follow the 7 Dark-First Utility DARK personality. No glassmorphism on the utility screens, rely on #09090B surface and #18181B surfaceSecondary tonal separation. Use the amber accent aggressively for primary actions and active states.

Typography constraint: Use Barlow Condensed (or equivalent high-impact condensed font loaded via expo-font) for all numeric displays (Calc output, Clock time, Timer digits) and DM Sans for standard UI text.
Calculator logic: Custom numpad must only contain 0-5. Calculations must be processed in base-6 logic, meaning after 5 comes 10, not 6.
Converter logic: Use a 'Convertible app' style sliding nested list rather than native modal pickers. Support Base conversions (Seximal <-> Decimal, Dozenal, Binary, Hexadecimal).

Converter prefixes & units: Embed the custom conversion rates provided in the prompt (e.g., 1 instant = 0.07716 sec, 1 thumb = 2.29867 inches, etc.) and handle Seximal prefixes (nifa-, kila-, etc. which represent powers of 6).

Time logic constraint: The clock shows base-6 time. 1 hour = 6^6 instants, 1 new minute = 6^4 instants (36 per hour), 1 new second = 6^2 instants (36 per new minute). The layout should take strong inspiration from iOS Clock (high contrast, circular timer progress, contextual end-times).
Do not use generic blue anywhere. The app must stay heavily anchored in obsidian grey and amber (#F59E0B).
